summary: Gensho Imanari (1925–2020) specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned his degrees, including a PhD in 1983, from Waseda University. He was an assistant professor at Kokushikan University (~1965–1972) and professor emeritus at Rissho University (1980–1996).
Genshu Watanabe (1869–1963) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at Toyo University and trained under Daiun Sogaku Harada, becoming his dharma heir.

Genzao (d. 1993) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950 and received instruction from traditional teachers Gyang rtse Rin po che (in 1948) and Kalu Rinpoche.

Geo Widengren (1907–1996) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies, earning his doctorate at Uppsala University under Henrik Samuel Nyberg. He held a professorship at Uppsala (1940–1973) and served as president of the IAHR (~1960–1970).

Geoff Childs is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, studying under Tsetan Chonjore, and held posts at the Australian National University and Washington University in St. Louis.

Geoffrey Barstow is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche and earned degrees from Hampshire College, Kathmandu University, and the University of Virginia before joining Oregon State University around 2013.

Geoffrey Goble is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Virginia and a PhD from Indiana University Bloomington, later serving as Assistant Professor at the University of Oklahoma (attested 2019).

Geoffrey Samuel is a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at Cambridge under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, Peter J. Wilson, and Edmund Leach, later holding professorships at Lancaster, Newcastle, and Cardiff universities.

Georg Buddruss (1929–2021) specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his doctorate under Paul Thieme at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1950–1954) and served as a professor at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1963–1995).

Georg Bühler (1837–1898) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen under Benfey, Sauppe, Curtius, and Ewald. He held professorships at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai (1863–1880) before taking a chair at the University of Vienna.
Georg Christoph Lichtenberg (1742–1799) studied at the University of Göttingen from ~1763 to 1769. He subsequently held an academic post at the University of Göttingen from ~1769 until 1799.

Georg Curtius (1820–1885) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Bonn and Humboldt University of Berlin under Ritschl, Lassen, Bopp, and Schlegel. He held professorships at Charles University (1849–1854), Kiel (1854–1862), and Leipzig University (1862–1885).

Georg Forster (1754–1794) was a scholar in Indology and other fields who studied at Saint Peter's School. He held posts at Vilnius University (1784–1787) and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1788–1792).

Georg Friedrich Grotefend (1775–1853) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He was educated at the Lessing-Gymnasium and studied at the University of Göttingen from ~1795 to 1797.

Georg Huth (1867–1906) was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Leipzig University (~1885–1890) and subsequently held an academic post at Humboldt University of Berlin from ~1891 to 1906.

Georg Kaibel (1849–1901) was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Breslau (~1879–1882), University of Rostock (~1882–1883), University of Greifswald (~1883–1886), and University of Göttingen (~1897–1901).

Georg Ludolf Dissen (1784–1837) was a linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1804–1807). He later held posts at the University of Marburg (~1812–1813) and the University of Göttingen (~1813–1837).

Georg Martin Dursch (1800–1881) studied theology, philosophy, and Indology at the University of Tübingen and the University of Paris under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. In 1829, he became a professor at the Johann-Vanotti-Gymnasium Ehingen.

Georg Morgenstierne (1892–1978) studied Indology and Iranian linguistics at Oslo, Bonn, and Berlin under Konow, Lüders, and Schulze. He served as a professor at the University of Gothenburg (1930–1937) and the University of Oslo (1937–1962).
Georg Simmel (1858–1918) was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin from ~1876 to 1881. He later held an academic post at Humboldt University of Berlin from ~1885 to 1914.
